ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Anti-Money Laundering and Countering Financing of Terrorism Act 2009 (NZ) (AML/CFT Act), sections 5, 6, and 9; Companies Act 1993 (NZ), sections 22-27 (name) and 87B-87H (significant controllers); Companies (Register of Significant Controllers) Amendment Act 2020 (NZ); Financial Markets Authority and Department of Internal Affairs AML/CFT Code of Practice 2024; Sanctions Act 2019 (NZ).

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: New Zealand Companies Office (Registrar of Companies)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille issued by the New Zealand Department of Internal Affairs (Authentication Unit) under the Hague Apostille Convention of 1961; no consular legalization for apostille states. For non-member states, a separate consular legalization via MFAT and the destination consulate applies (mutually exclusive with apostille, never sequential).

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Company Extract and Certificate of Good Standing
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille by the Department of Internal Affairs for recipient states party to the Apostille Convention; for non-Hague destinations, consular legalization through the Ministry of Foreign Affairs and Trade and the relevant embassy/consulate (parallel and mutually exclusive, never chained).

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Board Resolution Authorising the Incorporated Agent (Power of Attorney)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Board of Directors of NZ Ltd, signed before a New Zealand Notary Public
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarization by a New Zealand Notary Public, then Hague Apostille by the Department of Internal Affairs (or consular legalization if destination is a non-Hague state; the two methods are mutually exclusive and never combined sequentially).

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Shareholders and the incorporated entity of NZ Ltd
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Certified copy issued by the company secretary/board, followed by notarization and then Hague Apostille by the Department of Internal Affairs; consular legalization applies only for non-Hague states as a parallel and mutually exclusive route, not in sequence with apostille.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Licensed New Zealand bank (e.g., ANZ Bank New Zealand Limited, ASB Bank Limited, Bank of New Zealand, or Westpac New Zealand)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Original bank letter signed by an authorised bank officer, notarized if required, then Hague Apostille by the Department of Internal Affairs for apostille states; for non-Hague states, consular legalization via MFAT and the consulate is the sole alternative (mutually exclusive, never chained).

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: All proposed directors, shareholders, officers, and ultimate beneficial owners must be screened pre-incorporation against the New Zealand Sanctions Act 2019 consolidated list, the United Nations Security Council Consolidated List, and OFAC Specially Designated Nationals (SDN) list. Enhanced due diligence on politically exposed persons (PEPs) includes source-of-wealth inquiries, negative news search, and cross-reference through internationally recognised databases such as Thomson Reuters World-Check, Dow Jones Risk & Compliance, and LexisNexis. Ongoing screening is required at onboarding and subsequently every 90 days, with government-issued photographic ID, proof of address, and criminal background check from the country of residence.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: New Zealand Companies Office - Online Name Approval and Company Registration Portal (www.companiesoffice.govt.nz)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Names may be in English or Maori using Latin script; strict phonetic transliteration is required for any non-Latin script names. The Companies Office applies a four-tier naming convention: (1) the name must not be identical or almost identical to an existing reserved or registered name; (2) it must not contravene the Companies Act 1993 or other legislation; (3) it must not be offensive or contrary to public policy; and (4) it must not falsely imply any connection with the Crown, government, a local authority, or a regulated profession.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Within 20 working days of rejection, the applicant must file a written application for reconsideration with the Registrar of Companies, using Form NZ-28 (Name Reconsideration Request), articulating why the name meets the requirements of the Companies Act 1993 (sections 22-23). The Registrar must decide within 10 working days. If the rejection is upheld, the applicant may appeal to the District Court under section 23A within 20 working days. The applicant may simultaneously submit an alternative name reservation to avoid delay; extension of name reservation for a further 30 days is available upon online request before expiry.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: New Zealand law requires a registered office to be a physical street address in New Zealand, not a postal box. A virtual office that provides a physical street address and accepts government correspondence is permissible for registration and basic compliance, but local tax authorities (Inland Revenue Department) and banks will reject a commercial mailbox as the sole representation for a 3PL cross-dock e-commerce fulfillment operation. This industry demands demonstrable commercial substance: a leased or owned warehouse, dedicated staff, inventory management systems, and operational presence to support GST registration, payroll, customs bonded processing, and true economic activity. Thus, a virtual office may be used only as a registered address adjunct, never as the physical fulfillment site, and banks will require lease deeds and utility bills for the operational premises.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Risk Rating: Moderate (approximately 40% within the first 12 months of operation). Inspecting authorities include the Inland Revenue Department (IRD) for GST/PAYE audits and the Companies Office for statutory compliance. Checklist for unannounced on-site inspection: 1) external signage matching the registered company name; 2) staff presence and employment agreements; 3) valid lease or ownership deed for the premises; 4) operational inventory and racking/pallet systems; 5) loading dock and cross-dock equipment; 6) fire and health safety certificates; 7) waste management and environmental clearance for hazardous materials; and 8) IT infrastructure showing order management and warehouse management software. IRD may initiate field audits if GST refund claims exceed warehouse capacity indicators.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: New Zealand Companies Office (Ministry of Business, Innovation and Employment)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory fee under the Companies (Fees) Regulations 2020, NZD 150.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market benchmark for commercial registered office and resident agent services.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Appointment of New Zealand resident agent (for non-resident directors) - annual fee
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Licensed trustee company or corporate agent
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market benchmark per Foreign Direct Investment and Companies Act compliance.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Preparation of Articles of Association and Significant Controllers Register
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing corporate solicitor hourly rates (NZD 400-600 per hour); standard fixed fee for a multi-shareholder simple constitutional package.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Notarization and apostille/consular legalization bundle (5 documents)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Notary Public and Department of Internal Affairs (and MFAT for consular chain)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory apostille fee NZD 36 per document; notary fee NZD 120 per signature.
Bank tariff for standard reference letter (nil if account opened at same time).

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: IRD registration (Company Tax File Number, GST and PAYE application)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: No statutory government fee; agent handling fee (if outsourced) is NZD 250, market rate.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Companies Act 1993 (Public Act 1993 No 105), particularly sections 12 and 13 (registration and certificate of incorporation), sections 17-21 (constitution), sections 40-44 (share issue), sections 126-128 (director duties), section 151 (director residency), section 189 (registered office), and section 200 (financial records); Financial Reporting Act 2013; Tax Administration Act 1994
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registrar of Companies, New Zealand Companies Office, Ministry of Business, Innovation and Employment (MBIE)
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Application for Incorporation of a Company (Form 1 / Form INCN) under section 12 of the Companies Act 1993
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: None. The Companies Act 1993 and New Zealand regulations do not require any minimum paid-up capital. Ordinary shares may be issued at par or at a premium, and no blocked escrow or withheld capital account is mandated by law. Directors must ensure the company remains solvent before issuing shares or dividends in accordance with section 52 of the Companies Act 1993.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: BY UNANIMOUS WRITTEN RESOLUTION OF THE FIRST MEETING OF THE BOARD OF DIRECTORS OF 'NZ_LTD' (the Company), convened in accordance with the Company's constitution and Part 8 of the Companies Act 1993, held at the registered office of the Company on this day of [Month, Year]. The directors present, constituting a quorum, unanimously resolve and record as follows: (1) CONSTITUTION AND SHARE CAPITAL SUBSCRIPTION: The draft constitution tabled at this meeting is adopted as the constitution of the Company. The subscribers and shareholders accept and subscribe for Ordinary Shares with a par value of one New Zealand dollar each, in the numbers set out in the share register, at a consideration to be paid in cash within thirty days of the date of this resolution. The directors are authorized to allot, issue, and register the shares, and to issue share certificates. There being no minimum paid-up capital requirement, the Company may lawfully issue the shares without the establishment of a blocked or escrow account; (2) REGISTERED OFFICE ADOPTION: The registered office of the Company shall be [Registered Office Address], New Zealand, and the directors and officers are authorized to file the relevant notice with the Registrar of Companies and to maintain the office at which summonses and statutory notices may be served for no fewer than twenty hours per week as required by section 189 of the Companies Act 1993; (3) BANKING AUTHORIZATION: The board authorizes the opening of one or more transactional bank accounts with any registered bank in New Zealand and the use of Airwallex or similar non-bank licensed payment institutions for cross-border settlements and local ACH payment rails. The Chief Financial Officer, together with at least one other director, are appointed as authorized signatories with dual-approval control for transactions exceeding fifty thousand New Zealand dollars; (4) STATUTORY OFFICER AND OFFICER APPOINTMENTS: [Full Name] is appointed as sole executive director and managing director, [Full Name] is appointed as Chief Financial Officer, and [Full Name] of [Resident Agent Company] is appointed as New Zealand resident agent for service of process. The directors are authorized to execute all registrations, licensing applications, employment contracts, and tax filings necessary for the Company's cross-dock logistics business; (5) GENERAL POWERS: The directors are authorized to use electronic signatures under the Electronic Transactions Act 2002 and to delegate operational authority to the Chief Financial Officer. The chairman confirms that this resolution is valid, binding, and fully enforceable in accordance with the Companies Act 1993, and directs that the resolution be entered in the minute book.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: New Zealand Company Incorporation with the Companies Office
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registrar of Companies, New Zealand Companies Office (online portal: companies-register.companiesoffice.govt.nz)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Prepare and file the incorporation application through the New Zealand Companies Office online portal, using the exact legal name 'NZ_LTD' or a reserved available name. Enter the registered office address and principal place of business, director and shareholder particulars, and ISIC 5210 as the primary business activity. The incorporation form must be accompanied by signed consent to act as a director and a notice of registered office. The portal checks name availability, director eligibility, and address validity in real time. The applicant must ensure at least one director is a natural person resident in New Zealand or in Australia and serving as a director of a New Zealand company, in accordance with section 151 of the Companies Act 1993. After validation, the prescribed incorporation fee is paid by credit card. The Registrar will issue the Certificate of Incorporation and the New Zealand Business Number (NZBN), completing statutory formation.
required_dossiers: Completed Form 1 / Form INCN online application
Certificate of name approval or consent to use the name
Signed Consent to Act as Director for each director
Notice of Registered Office form
Identity and residential address proof for each director and shareholder
Proposed constitution, if a bespoke constitution is adopted
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registrar suspends or queries the application, log into the Companies Office portal and respond in writing within ten working days. If the company name is refused, reserve and submit a new available name. If consent forms are invalid, obtain fresh signed consents from all directors. After the cure is completed, the Registrar will reissue the certificate; if the query is not resolved, the applicant may seek administrative review under the Companies Act 1993.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: First Board Meeting, Share Allotment and Statutory Governance Records
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Board of Directors of NZ_LTD, with post-filing records maintained at the registered office and any required share allotment notice filed with the Companies Office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Convene the first board meeting of the newly incorporated company. The directors adopt the constitution, subscribe and allot ordinary shares, approve the opening of bank accounts, appoint statutory officers, and confirm the registered office. The board must prepare and retain signed minutes, share register, director consent forms, and register of charges. If shares are issued for non-cash consideration, a valuation report must be tabled and an appropriate resolution passed. The share allotment must be recorded in the share register and any required return of allotment filed with the Registrar of Companies. The resolutions passed at the meeting constitute the fundamental governance record of the company and should be dated and signed by the chairperson. All corporate records must be kept at the registered office.
required_dossiers: Signed pro-forma first board resolution
Share register and ledger
Consent to Act as Director forms
Certificate of Incorporation from step 1
Directors' and shareholders' identity documents
Minutes of the first meeting signed by the chairperson
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registrar raises a query on the share allotment or governance filing, file a corrective statement within ten working days. If a director withdraws consent, appoint a replacement director by board resolution and file the applicable notice with the Companies Office. Maintain a remedy log to keep governance records aligned with the public register.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Tax Registration with Inland Revenue and Banking / Payment Rails Activation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Inland Revenue Department (IRD) via MyIR; registered commercial banks in New Zealand; Airwallex or licensed non-bank payment providers; AML/CFT supervisor under the Department of Internal Affairs
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After incorporation, apply to Inland Revenue for an IRD number. Initiate the application through the Companies Office portal or IRD MyIR platform. If annual taxable supplies are expected to exceed NZD 60,000, register for Goods and Services Tax (GST). Register as an employer for PAYE if hiring staff, and adopt the KiwiSaver rules. Open a business transactional bank account with a registered New Zealand bank. The bank will require the certificate of incorporation, IRD number, and identity or address verification for all directors and beneficial owners. For cross-border payments and local ACH settlement, complete Airwallex entity onboarding using the same corporate documentary package and link the operating bank account. Maintain all AML/CFT records in accordance with the Anti-Money Laundering and Countering Financing of Terrorism Act 2009.
required_dossiers: Certificate of Incorporation and NZBN certificate
IRD number application confirmation
GST and PAYE registration forms, where applicable
Certified identity documents for directors and shareholders with beneficial ownership over 25 percent
Certificate of registered office
Business plan or projected revenue statement for the banking and payment provider
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the IRD number application remains pending, contact the IRD Business Helpline or use MyIR secure mail to resolve identity verification deficiencies. If the bank account application is delayed, provide certified English translations for non-English documents and amend the corporate documentary pack. If the AML/CFT supervisor asks questions, update the business risk assessment and beneficial ownership register with a written response.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Resource Consent and Cross-Dock Warehousing Operating License
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Territorial Authority (City or District Council) under the Resource Management Act 1991, and the Regional Council for trade waste and stormwater discharge permits
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Determine the zoning and land use status of the proposed cross-dock facility. Submit a resource consent application for warehousing, cross-dock logistics, and storage operations if the district plan does not classify the activity as a permitted activity. If the activity is a permitted activity, obtain a Certificate of Compliance confirming that no resource consent is required. Where the facility generates trade waste, apply for a trade waste discharge permit from the local council or regional council. Engage a qualified planner to prepare an Assessment of Environmental Effects (AEE) covering traffic generation, noise, stormwater, and hazardous substance storage. The process will include consultation with adjacent property owners if the activity is discretionary. Follow the statutory processing timeframe under the RMA 1991, and after consent is issued satisfy all conditions concerning operating hours, loading dock use, landscaping, and stormwater capture.
required_dossiers: Certificate of title or executed lease for the cross-dock facility
Site plan and floor plan showing loading docks, racks, offices, and fire escape routes
Assessment of Environmental Effects (AEE) prepared by a planning consultant
Traffic and parking impact assessment
Stormwater and trade waste discharge calculations
Noise assessment pertaining to machinery and truck movements
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the resource consent application is publicly notified or challenged by the council, submit supplementary AEE information and expert evidence within the statutory timeframe. If consent is declined by the territorial authority, appeal to the Environment Court under section 120 of the Resource Management Act 1991 within fifteen working days of the decision. For minor deficiencies such as incomplete plans or unpaid fees, the council will issue a formal notice allowing the applicant to cure the missing information.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Civil Defence Fire Safety and Workplace Health and Safety Clearance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Fire and Emergency New Zealand (FENZ), WorkSafe New Zealand, and the local Territorial Authority building official under the Building Act 2004
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Engage a licensed building consultant to inspect the warehouse premises and verify that the building is safe for use as a cross-dock and storage facility. Apply for or transfer the Building Warrant of Fitness under the Building Act 2004, and ensure all specified systems such as fire alarms, sprinklers, emergency lighting, and fire doors are independently inspected by an independently qualified person (IQP). Submit an application to Fire and Emergency New Zealand for approval of the Fire Evacuation Scheme. Where the facility handles hazardous substances, complete HSNO location compliance reporting to WorkSafe. Prepare a general risk assessment and health and safety plan under the Health and Safety at Work Act 2015. Obtain a structural load clearance from a chartered professional engineer for racking, mezzanine floors, dock levellers, and any refrigeration plant. All certificates and safety notices must be displayed and retained on site.
required_dossiers: Building Warrant of Fitness application or transfer form
IQP inspection reports for specified fire safety systems
Fire Evacuation Scheme application submitted to FENZ
Structural load capacity certificate from a chartered professional engineer
WorkSafe notification form and health and safety risk assessment
Hazardous Substances Inventory if chemicals or aerosols are stored
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Fire Evacuation Scheme is not approved, revise the evacuation plan and resubmit to FENZ. If the Building Warrant of Fitness is non-compliant, instruct the building owner to rectify specified system deficiencies and obtain a new certificate from the IQP. WorkSafe improvement notices must be remediated and verified by a health and safety assessor before operations can continue.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Territorial Authority (City or District Council) under the Resource Management Act 1991; Regional Council for trade waste and stormwater discharge permits; Fire and Emergency New Zealand; WorkSafe New Zealand
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Cross-Dock Warehouse Land Use Resource Consent; Trade Waste Discharge Permit; Fire Evacuation Scheme Approval; Building Warrant of Fitness

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Environmental Protection Authority (EPA) New Zealand, with plan administration by the Regional Council under the Resource Management Act 1991
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Tier 2 Controlled Activity: Land Use Resource Consent with a qualitative Assessment of Environmental Effects (AEE). A full national Environment Impact Assessment report is not automatically required for an ISIC 5210 warehouse unless the site is in a sensitive natural environment or stores hazardous substances above HSNO notification thresholds.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Wastewater and trade waste discharge to sewer: pH 6.0 to 9.0, biochemical oxygen demand (BOD) not exceeding 300 mg/L, total suspended solids (TSS) not exceeding 100 mg/L, oil and grease not exceeding 15 mg/L. Stormwater discharge: total suspended solids below 50 mg/L with no visible oil sheen. Hazardous substance storage must comply with the Health and Safety at Work (Hazardous Substances) Regulations 2017, including approved location certification for quantities above 1,000 kg. Refrigerant systems must comply with the Ozone Layer Protection Act 1996 with leakage rates below one percent of charge per annum.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Mandatory Building Warrant of Fitness under the Building Act 2004 for fire suppression systems, sprinklers, emergency warning systems, and fire doors; approved Fire Evacuation Scheme under the Fire and Emergency New Zealand Act 2017; WorkSafe notification and prescribed workplace safety policies under the Health and Safety at Work Act 2015; structural load clearance from a chartered professional engineer for racking, mezzanine floors, dock levellers, and heavy-duty storage areas.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Inland Revenue Department (Te Tari Tāke), New Zealand, operating the myIR secure online tax portal; customs control is administered separately by the New Zealand Customs Service for export declarations.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: For a foreign non-resident entity seeking a New Zealand IRD number and GST registration: (1) Determine New Zealand GST registration status using the NZD 60,000 annual taxable turnover test, including any obligation for non-resident suppliers of remote services or low-value imported goods. (2) Submit the prescribed Non-Resident Company IRD Number Application to Inland Revenue, providing certified copies of the certificate of incorporation, constitutional documents, board and ownership details, and the entity's overseas tax residence information. (3) If appointed, name a New Zealand agent or authorised representative for service of notices and tax communications. (4) Inland Revenue issues an IRD number; use that number and myIR credentials to lodge a GST registration application under the Goods and Services Tax Act 1985, selecting the applicable return filing frequency (monthly, two-monthly, or six-monthly). (5) Maintain bank account details in myIR, GST records, and export evidence; the entity may need a New Zealand Business Number (NZBN) only if operating a business in New Zealand, but this is separate from income tax and GST registration. (6) Where formal tax residence is required, apply for a tax residence certificate through myIR after finalising director and head-office facts under the Income Tax Act 2007.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: None for GST. New Zealand has no general check-the-box entity classification and no GST group election for cross-border passive holding companies; income tax carries a look-through company (LTC) election for qualifying New Zealand close companies, subject to strict New Zealand-resident ownership criteria, but this does not alter the indirect tax classification of an NZ Limited Company.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: NZD 60,000 of taxable supplies in a 12-month period; non-resident remote-service suppliers to New Zealand consumers and non-resident suppliers of low-value imported goods are also subject to the same NZD 60,000 annual turnover threshold.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: No real-time tax authority clearance, anti-fraud digital stamping, or mandatory electronic invoicing. New Zealand operates on a self-issuance GST invoice model. Taxable invoices must contain the supplier's name and NZ GST/IRD number, invoice date, supplier and recipient details, description, quantity, price, GST amount, and must be issued within 28 calendar days after supply. E-invoicing via the Peppol network is voluntary. GST records must be kept in either paper or electronic form for seven years.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: A supply of goods is zero-rated where the supplier exports the goods from New Zealand, or where a customer receives the goods in New Zealand and exports them within 28 days, provided the export is evidenced to the satisfaction of Inland Revenue. Services related to exported goods and qualifying remote or offshore services supplied to a non-resident customer may also be zero-rated under the Goods and Services Tax Act 1985. The supplier must hold commercial and customs documentation proving the goods physically left New Zealand and that the transaction was a genuine cross-border supply; for cross-border e-commerce fulfilment, the contract must identify the overseas principal or buyer and the overseas final destination.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs export declaration (export entry) accepted by the New Zealand Customs Service, lodged through the Trade Single Window or approved integrated cargo system
Bill of lading or airway bill evidencing shipment from a New Zealand port or airport
Commercial invoice and purchase order identifying the offshore customer and final overseas delivery address
Packing list and courier or carrier proof of delivery records
Customs or shipping warehouse evidence showing the goods were not redirected back into New Zealand consumption

Bank and foreign exchange records, such as SWIFT MT103 or NZD inward remittance statements, showing payment from the offshore counterparty; an Inward Remittance Certificate is not a New Zealand statutory customs requirement
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Inland Revenue can deny zero-rating and assess GST at 15% on the original supply where export evidence is incomplete, false, or generated solely to obtain zero-rating. The taxpayer must then pay output tax, use-of-money interest from the original GST due date, late payment penalties, and shortfall penalties ranging from 20% for a failure to exercise reasonable care up to 150% for evasion. Criminal liability or prosecution may arise for knowingly producing false customs or export documentation, with mandatory record retention of seven years.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: New Zealand operates a fully liberalised, free-floating foreign exchange regime under the Reserve Bank of New Zealand Act 1989, with no restrictions on current account or capital account convertibility. The New Zealand dollar (NZD) trades freely in global interbank markets, and there are no exchange control approvals, no mandatory central bank notification for inward or outward transfers, and no surrender requirements on export proceeds. Profits, dividends, and capital repatriation may be remitted without prior regulatory consent. The only statutory obligations are general AML/CFT reporting under the Anti-Money Laundering and Countering Financing of Terrorism Act 2009 and tax compliance. For a non-resident owned NZ limited company engaged in cross-border 3PL fulfillment, dividends can be declared under NZ GAAP and paid via SWIFT MT103 without FX allocation constraints. Inbound equity injections require Companies Office share allotment filings; no central bank permission is needed. The practical constraint is that cross-border payment rails must be priced against NZD liquidity in the offshore NDF market; APAC e-commerce settlement currency mixes create natural hedging opportunities. Overall, the jurisdiction poses minimal FX friction to treasury operations.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: No statutory surrender rules apply in New Zealand. Export foreign currency receipts may be retained offshore or repatriated freely in full (100% maintainable) with no statutory conversion ratio and no mandatory deadline. The only duties are accurate accounting records for tax filing and standard AML/CFT transaction monitoring for inbound remittances.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Airwallex (NZ) Limited holds a New Zealand Financial Service Provider registration and is legally permitted to service NZ corporate clients for multi-currency settlement, local ACH direct debit, and global payout rails. Viability is rated Medium-High: EMIs are not barred in New Zealand, but they cannot act as the sole bank for statutory capital verification or provide committed lending facilities. The recommended treasury architecture is to pair a Tier-1 domestic bank (ANZ or BNZ) for the capital escrow and primary NZD operating account with a regulated EMI for high-frequency cross-border ecommerce settlement, subject to the EMI's own AML/CFT programme being approved by the relationship bank and mirror transfers documented in the operating agreement.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: In New Zealand, physical presence is generally required at initial corporate account opening. RealMe verified identity supports remote customer due diligence for natural persons, but for a corporate entity with non-resident directors, major banks mandate at least one director or authorised signatory to attend an in-branch interview in Auckland, Wellington, or Christchurch. Remote notarised and consular certified identity packs may be accepted on a case-by-case basis, yet on-screen video interviews are not universally accepted for non-resident-controlled customers without an existing banking relationship. Statutory directors listed on the NZ Companies Office register face a de facto physical presence requirement for the first operational account, with a secondary remote consular proxy route available only through the bank's private banking division.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Beneficial ownership opacity where indirect foreign shareholding is held through a trust or intermediate holding company
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certified trust deed or registered share register tracing each individual beneficial owner above 25%; certificate of incorporation for each intermediate holding entity; notarised passports and source-of-wealth statements for all ultimate beneficial owners; written attestation from the NZ director confirming the control chain has not changed within 90 days.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-frequency cross-border ecommerce settlement volume creating a money-laundering concealment pattern
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Executed commercial fulfilment contracts with at least two anchor merchants; six months of independent payment gateway statements (Stripe, Shopify Payments, or PayPal) reconciling gross settlement flows to logistics manifests; warehouse management system inventory-to-order reconciliation reports; a narrated business model memo explaining chargebacks, refunds, and intercompany commission flows.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Sanctions and restricted-goods exposure because cross-dock operators handle goods for third-party merchants
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Commodity Harmonised System (HS) code list for all stored inventory; contractual clause prohibiting handling of goods subject to NZ sanctions or the Russia/Ukraine restrictive measures; counterparty screening logs showing negative-news checks against the NZ Consolidated Sanctions List and OFAC listings at or below 0.1% threshold; annual AML/CFT compliance officer sign-off.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unclear commercial rationale for routing global ecommerce settlement through an NZ entity when vendors and sales platforms are offshore
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Group structure chart showing the NZ entity's substantive role as order fulfilment and cross-dock operator; board minutes approving the NZ logistics hub strategy; OECD-aligned transfer pricing documentation confirming a market-derived margin for the NZ entity; evidence of 24-month warehouse lease or ownership in a New Zealand distribution site.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Equity capital is remitted by SWIFT MT103 from the parent or shareholder account to the NZ entity's capital escrow account at ANZ or BNZ. The payment message must show the remitter as the actual registered shareholder, the beneficiary as 'NZ_LTD', and the OECD purpose code for direct investment (e.g., Code 1000 equity capital or equivalent). No central bank approval is required in New Zealand, but the bank will reflect the inward credit as capital and request the Companies Office share allotment filing (AR30) to complete capital verification. A statutory declaration or New Zealand chartered accountant confirmation letter may supplement audit review of the capital injection.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Trade settlements for cross-dock fulfilment should use SWIFT MT103 high-value telegraphic transfers for supplier payments under USD 250,000, Commercial Letters of Credit for confirmed large purchase orders where the issuing bank adds an irrevocable payment undertaking, and Documentary Collections (D/P or D/A) for low-risk repeat shipments with established counterparties. Local-currency disbursements in NZD and AUD are cleared through the NZ Clearing Direct Entry (ACH2) and the Bulk Electronic Clearing System; USD, EUR, and CNY legs execute via correspondent banks on the SWIFT FIN network with standard 48-hour processing and strict reference to underlying invoices in the payment narrative.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Plain-vanilla FX Forwards up to 12 months tenor against NZD/USD and NZD/CNY
European-style FX Options for non-linear exposure on APAC settlement currencies
Cross-currency swaps (CCS) for matched funding of offshore warehouse operating leases
Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) - legally permitted but generally unnecessary because NZD is fully convertible

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Return of the Company under Companies Act 1993
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registrar of Companies, Companies Office, Ministry of Business, Innovation and Employment (MBIE), New Zealand
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually on the anniversary of incorporation (annual return date), with a 35-working-day grace period; e.g., incorporated 15 June, filing must occur by no later than the 35th working day after 15 June each year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing attracts incremental Companies Office late fees; persistent failure results in a Registrar's notice of intention to remove the company under section 328 of the Companies Act 1993, administrative strike-off, loss of the registered name, and Crown treatment of unclaimed property.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual income tax return (IR4) with applicable financial statements and tax reconciliation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Inland Revenue Department (IRD) / Te Tari Taake, New Zealand
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: For a standard 31 March balance date, the IR4 return must be filed no later than 7 July following year-end; approved tax agents may use the extended IRD filing date calendar
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing penalty (from NZD 250, plus escalation of NZD 50 per month) and use-of-money interest on underpaid provisional tax; directors may be personally liable for penalties and prosecution for persistent tax default.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Goods and Services Tax (GST) return for the GST-registered overseas-warehouse order-fulfilment business
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Inland Revenue Department (IRD) / Te Tari Taake, New Zealand
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: If the taxable period is annual, filing is required within one month after the balance date of the GST period (or the later IRD-specified due date); monthly/two-monthly/six-monthly filers must follow their IRD allocation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalty (LFP) of NZD 50 per month up to NZD 750, incremental late payment penalties, and use-of-money interest; IRD may issue an amended/assessed return where non-filing continues.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Statutory financial statements and auditor's report (if audit threshold is met or not validly waived by unanimous shareholder resolution)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Board/shareholders; the audited statements must be available at the company's registered office and filed with the Registrar of Companies when the company is required to do so
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 5 months after balance date, unless a later date is validly approved; the directors are personally responsible for timely preparation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Directors may be fined up to NZD 10,000 under Companies Act 1993 for failure to prepare financial statements; continued non-compliance can be restrained by shareholder application or by the Registrar.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: A certified independent audit is mandatory unless the company qualifies as a 'small company' and shareholders unanimously resolve to waive the audit. Under the Companies Act 1993 and Financial Reporting Act 2013, a company is not small (and therefore audit is compulsory) when, in any two of the three immediately preceding accounting periods (or all periods, if fewer), it meets any two of: (a) total consolidated assets NZD 3,000,000 or more; (b) total consolidated annual revenue NZD 6,000,000 or more; (c) 12 or more full-time-equivalent employees. Audit is also compulsory for issuers, overseas companies, entities with public accountability, and where shareholders holding 5% of voting rights deliver a written audit demand under section 200 of the Companies Act 1993.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: New Zealand IFRS (Tier 1) or New Zealand IFRS with Reduced Disclosure Regime (Tier 2) for for-profit entities under the External Reporting Board framework (NZ IFRS / NZ GAAP); small non-reporting entities may apply the simplified reporting standards permitted by XRB A1, while all consolidated reports of larger entities follow IFRS as issued in New Zealand.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The Companies Act 1993 requires every company to keep an accurate Register of Members and Register of Directors. The annual return filed with the Companies Office updates shareholder and director details as at the annual return date. Share allotments must be reported via a Return of Allotment within 20 working days. Share transfers are recorded in the Register of Members and are reflected in the next annual return; New Zealand does not maintain a separate public UBO filing, but AML/CFT obligations require the company's agent and/or New Zealand directors to identify and retain current beneficial-owner information and to update it whenever material changes occur.

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 400 - USD 1,500 per annum for registered office, annual return compliance, and corporate secretarial agent services in New Zealand
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 4,000 - USD 18,000 per annum for a certified statutory audit of a cross-dock / 3PL overseas fulfilment entity under NZ IFRS/NZ GAAP, depending on transaction volume, payroll, and intercompany balances.

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 28% flat corporate income tax rate (Income Tax Act 2007, Schedule 1, Part A, clause 3)
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No statutory tax holidays are available in New Zealand. The effective burden is reduced by the full imputation credit system, which eliminates economic double taxation on distributed profits, and by a refundable 15% R&D tax credit on qualifying expenditure. Losses may be carried forward indefinitely to achieve tax deferral. There is no general capital gains tax, although gains on depreciable property and timber are taxable. For exported goods and certain cross-border services, GST is zero-rated at 15%. The aggregate tax burden on a distribution to a Chinese parent company is 28% corporate tax plus 5% DTA-rate dividend NRWT, producing a combined effective rate of 31.6%.
corporate_income_tax_regime.tax_loss_carryforward_limit_years: Indefinite (no statutory expiry). Under section IA 4 of the Income Tax Act 2007, losses are carried forward indefinitely provided the 49% shareholding continuity test is satisfied throughout the continuity period, or the business continuity test is met.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: IR4 Company Income Tax Return; mandatory electronic filing through the Inland Revenue 'myIR' secure online portal or via an approved third-party software / XML-API gateway.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual. The income year is the 12-month period ending 31 March or an approved non-standard balance date (e.g., 30 June, 31 December). Provisional tax is paid in three instalments during the income year; for the standard 31 March balance date, instalments fall on 28 August, 15 January and 7 May.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: For a standard 31 March balance date: terminal tax is due on 7 April of the following income year, and the IR4 return must be filed by 7 July following the balance date. IRD-approved tax agent clients receive an extension of time to 31 March of the following year. For non-standard balance dates, the IR4 is due on the 6th month after balance date and terminal tax is due by the 15th day of the 12th month after balance date.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Sales, trading income, warehousing and order-fulfilment fees, handling charges, storage revenue and ancillary logistics income derived in New Zealand.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report all New Zealand-source gross receipts. A company incorporated in New Zealand is a tax resident and must declare worldwide income; foreign-source income is separately calculated only where a specific exemption applies.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gross interest income received, including intercompany lending income and cash-pool credit balances.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Declare gross interest. Any foreign withholding tax credits claimed must be supported by the relevant DTA residence certificate and reconciled in the tax reconciliation statement.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Dividend income received from New Zealand-resident and non-resident companies.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Include only taxable dividends after applying the imputation rules. Fully imputed and exempt intercorporate dividends are excluded, and the imputation credit account balance must be reconciled.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: All other assessable income, including foreign exchange gains, insurance recoveries, management fee recharges and any recharacterised income from transfer pricing adjustments.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Include arm's length recharge income from offshore affiliates. The tax director must ensure the full amount corresponds to the transfer pricing file maintained for the entity.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Total assessable income for the income year, being the sum of Boxes 1 to 4.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Must reconcile to the financial statements, management accounts and general ledger of the New Zealand entity.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Total deductions, including warehouse lease costs, personnel expenses, freight, outsourced 3PL subcontractor charges, depreciation, interest on intercompany funding and other operating expenses.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-deductible payments must be eliminated. Interest deductions are limited by the New Zealand thin capitalisation rules: worldwide group debt cannot exceed 75% of worldwide assets and New Zealand group debt cannot exceed 60% of New Zealand assets.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net accounting profit or loss before tax as reported in the statutory financial statements.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Base amount taken directly from financial statements prepared under New Zealand IFRS or the NZ Accounting Standards Framework.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax adjustments: add-back of non-deductible expenditure such as entertainment, fines, penalties, non-commercial intercompany charges, and elimination of non-taxable accounting income.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Add back any shortfall in arm's length pricing identified by the tax director. A voluntary transfer pricing adjustment made before filing reduces the risk of shortfall penalties.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable income after setting off brought-forward tax losses.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Verify the shareholder continuity test for every day of the year or the business continuity test before utilising losses; failure of either test permanently forfeits the losses.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Provisional tax paid and resident withholding tax credits attached.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Reconcile against the myIR provisional tax schedule. Use-of-money interest is automatically imposed where provisional tax instalments are underpaid.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Terminal tax payable or refund due, calculated at 28% of taxable income less all credits.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For the standard 31 March balance date, terminal tax is due 7 April following the income year. Unpaid tax attracts late payment penalties of 1% immediately, 4% plus 1% per month thereafter, and daily use-of-money interest.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing penalty: NZD 250 for companies with annual gross income below NZD 5 million, and NZD 500 for companies with annual gross income of NZD 5 million or more. Late payment penalty: 1% of unpaid tax immediately on the due date, a further 4% after seven days, and 1% per full calendar month thereafter. Use-of-money interest is charged at the Inland Revenue underpayment rate, approximately 8.59% per annum for the 2025 tax year, compounded daily. Additional shortfall penalties of 20% to 150% apply for incorrect tax positions.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 30% statutory Non-Resident Withholding Tax (NRWT) on dividends paid by a New Zealand company to a non-resident shareholder (section NF 2, Income Tax Act 2007). Treaty relief reduces the rate to 15% on portfolio dividends and to 5% on substantial-holding dividends under the NZ-China DTA where the beneficial owner is a company holding at least 25% of the capital of the payer. Under the NZ-Australia DTA, the rate is 15% generally and 5% where the beneficial owner is a company holding at least 10% of the voting power.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: The New Zealand payer applies the reduced treaty rate only after the non-resident recipient obtains a Tax Residence Certificate (TRC) from its home tax authority and delivers it to the New Zealand company, together with a declaration of beneficial ownership. The New Zealand company must retain the TRC and, where required, apply to Inland Revenue for reduced-NRWT approval using the appropriate exemption application (IR58 series). NRWT returns are filed on IR67, with payment due by the 20th day after the month in which the dividend is paid. For interest payments, an Approved Issuer Levy election (IR67B) substitutes the 2% AIL for NRWT where the borrower is an approved issuer. If tax is over-withheld, the non-resident may file an IR3NR non-resident income tax return to claim a refund, attaching the TRC, dividend vouchers and interest certificates.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Interest: 15% statutory NRWT, reduced to 10% under the NZ-China DTA and most other double tax agreements, or to 2% Approved Issuer Levy where the New Zealand borrower is an approved issuer and the payment qualifies for AIL. Royalties: 15% statutory NRWT on payments for the use of intellectual property, including software license fees, franchise fees, trademarks and technical know-how; the rate is reduced to 10% under the NZ-China DTA. Approved Issuer Levy does not apply to royalties.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: New Zealand does not impose a statutory monetary threshold requiring preparation of a transfer pricing file, but Inland Revenue practice establishes administrative safe-harbour thresholds: related-party goods transactions of NZD 4 million or more per annum; related-party services of NZD 1 million or more per annum; and related-party financial arrangements of NZD 10 million or more in aggregate principal. Multinational enterprise groups with global consolidated revenue above NZD 1 billion are expected to hold Master File and Local File documentation aligned with the OECD Transfer Pricing Guidelines for related party transactions exceeding these thresholds.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: New Zealand does not operate a Caribbean-style Economic Substance Regulations (ESR) statute. Substance is nevertheless enforced through the general anti-avoidance rule in section BG 1 of the Income Tax Act 2007, the thin capitalisation rules in Part FE, the CFC and FIF attribution regimes, and the shareholder continuity rules governing loss utilisation. A cross-border fulfillment and cross-dock subsidiary must demonstrate genuine commercial substance: physical warehousing premises in New Zealand, locally engaged or supervised operations staff, executed logistics contracts with independent third parties, and substantive board decision-making in New Zealand. Absent such substance, Inland Revenue may recharacterise the arrangement, reattribute profit to New Zealand, disallow intercompany deductions and apply reconstruction penalties.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Knowingly providing a false tax return, omitting fulfillment and cross-dock revenue, destroying or falsifying records, instructing customers to pay offshore bank accounts, or using shell payees to suppress taxable income of the New Zealand company, contrary to sections 143A and 143B of the Tax Administration Act 1994.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Evasion shortfall penalty of 150% of the tax avoided; penalty for insufficiently maintained records of up to NZD 12,000; criminal conviction carrying a fine of up to NZD 50,000 and imprisonment of up to 5 years.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and senior officers who directed, instigated or assisted the evasion are personally liable for the company tax shortfall under section 149 of the Tax Administration Act 1994. The corporate veil will be pierced where the company is a mere facade; directors face civil restitution, asset freezing, travel bans pending offshore asset investigation, and imprisonment upon criminal conviction.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating the New Zealand limited company as a mere booking or reinvoicing vehicle with no warehouse, staff, logistics operations or local decision-making authority, while attributing the full fulfilment margin to an offshore affiliate; such arrangement contravenes section BG 1 of the Income Tax Act 2007 and the arm's length standard in sections GC 6 to GC 13B.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Inland Revenue may reconstruct the arrangement to deny deductions, reattribute profit to New Zealand, impose a shortfall penalty of 40% for an unacceptable tax position or 100% for an abusive tax position, and apply NRWT of 30% on deemed dividends arising from recharacterised payments.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be personally assessed for the reconstructed company tax under section 149 of the Tax Administration Act 1994, disqualified under the Companies Act 1993, and subjected to asset freezing orders and travel bans where offshore asset-stripping or phoenix company conduct is established.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Transfer Pricing Misstatement and Thin Capitalisation Breach
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Setting intercompany warehouse handling fees, management service charges, royalties or shareholder loan interest at non-arm's length levels, or funding the New Zealand entity with excessive debt exceeding the 75% worldwide group / 60% New Zealand group debt-to-asset ratios under Part FE of the Income Tax Act 2007.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Inland Revenue adjusts taxable income to the arm's length result, disallows interest deductions on the excessive debt component, and applies a shortfall penalty of up to 40% for an unacceptable tax position or up to 150% for evasion; imputation credit account penalties of 10% to 20% are separately imposed for incorrect credit allocations.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who signed false transfer pricing declarations or directed the artificial funding structure are jointly and severally liable for the resulting tax shortfall; in insolvency, directors may be assessed for tax debts under section 300 of the Companies Act 1993 for reckless or fraudulent trading, with unlimited personal liability and disqualification.
